data.body: Starting evidence (read from source at b4e0d01b649, not yet tested on Windows): the product-side literal is the read-freshness throttle marker in `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py` `_sync_marker_age` (`f"/tmp/.ticket-sync-{md5[:12]}"`), opened for read there and for write later in `ensure_fresh`. On Windows `/tmp` is drive-relative and usually absent, so the read returns age 9999 and the write fails inside the best-effort `except`, which would mean the 60-second fetch throttle never engages and every read fetches. Test-side copies of the literal: `tests/unit/test_read_freshness_git_spawns.py:99`, `tests/unit/test_read_freshness_parity.py:139`, `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py:152`, `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py:91`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_fresh_ac_material.py:47`, `tests/interfaces/store/sync_contention_harness.py:46`. Design point for the fix: `tempfile.gettempdir()` honours `TMPDIR`, so two processes with different `TMPDIR` would stop sharing one throttle on POSIX; a marker under the tracker's git dir avoids that. Expose the path through one helper the tests import instead of re-deriving it.
